general_contracting.insurance_bond: General liability insurance of at least $500,000, plus workers' compensation if the contractor has employees.
general_contracting.summary: Rhode Island law requires anyone doing residential or commercial construction work to register with the Contractors' Registration and Licensing Board. A 2025 law (R.I. Gen. Laws chapter 5-65.4) will also require a residential contractor license for building new homes and structural remodeling starting January 1, 2028.

hvac.agency: Rhode Island Department of Labor and Training, Division of Professional Regulation
hvac.summary: Rhode Island licenses pipefitters, refrigeration technicians, and sheet metal workers, the trades that cover HVAC work, through the Department of Labor and Training. Homeowners can search trade licenses online by trade, name, or license number.

legal.summary: Rhode Island attorneys are admitted by the Supreme Court and file annual registration through the court's attorney portal. The Judiciary's public Attorney Search provides attorney information, with registration questions handled by the Supreme Court Clerk's Office.

plumbing.agency: Rhode Island Department of Labor and Training, Division of Professional Regulation
plumbing.summary: Rhode Island licenses plumbers through the Department of Labor and Training's Division of Professional Regulation. Licenses can be checked with the division's online trade license search.

roofing.agency: Rhode Island Contractors' Registration and Licensing Board (CRLB), Department of Business Regulation
roofing.insurance_bond: Commercial roofing license: general liability insurance of at least $2,000,000, plus workers' compensation if the contractor has employees.
roofing.summary: Rhode Island requires a Commercial Roofing License from the CRLB for commercial or industrial roofing work; it does not cover residential buildings with four or fewer dwelling units. Residential roofers must still register with the CRLB as contractors.

electrical.agency: South Carolina Residential Builders Commission (SC LLR)
electrical.insurance_bond: A bond is required when work for an individual property owner exceeds $5,000.
electrical.summary: For residential work, South Carolina's Residential Builders Commission issues residential electrician licenses after an exam. The license applies to residential specialty work exceeding $500; commercial mechanical work falls under the SC Contractor's Licensing Board.

general_contracting.agency: South Carolina Residential Builders Commission (SC LLR)
general_contracting.summary: South Carolina requires a Residential Builder license from the Residential Builders Commission when the cost of a residential job exceeds $5,000. Regulated commercial construction over $10,000 requires a General or Mechanical Contractor license from the SC Contractor's Licensing Board.
general_contracting.threshold: residential work when the cost of the undertaking exceeds $5,000; commercial construction over $10,000

hvac.agency: South Carolina Residential Builders Commission (SC LLR)
hvac.insurance_bond: A bond is required when work for an individual property owner exceeds $5,000.
hvac.summary: For residential work, South Carolina's Residential Builders Commission issues HVAC (heating and air conditioning installer and repairer) licenses after an exam. The license applies to residential specialty work exceeding $500; commercial mechanical work falls under the SC Contractor's Licensing Board.

legal.agency: South Carolina Judicial Branch / South Carolina Bar
legal.summary: The South Carolina Judicial Branch runs a public attorney search covering attorneys licensed to practice law in South Carolina. You can search by first name, last name, or bar number.

plumbing.agency: South Carolina Residential Builders Commission (SC LLR)
plumbing.insurance_bond: A bond is required when work for an individual property owner exceeds $5,000.
plumbing.summary: For residential work, South Carolina's Residential Builders Commission issues residential plumber licenses after an exam. The license applies to residential specialty work exceeding $500; commercial mechanical work falls under the SC Contractor's Licensing Board.

roofing.agency: South Carolina Residential Builders Commission (SC LLR)
roofing.insurance_bond: A $5,000 surety bond must be on file before doing work over $5,000 total cost (labor and materials) on a project.
roofing.summary: Residential roofers in South Carolina register with the Residential Builders Commission as residential specialty contractors (Roofing classification) for jobs over $500. Commercial roofing is licensed by the SC Contractor's Licensing Board.

electrical.agency: South Dakota Electrical Commission (Department of Labor and Regulation)
electrical.insurance_bond: Electrical contractors must provide a $10,000 undertaking and public liability insurance of at least $100,000 per occurrence and $300,000 aggregate (or a $300,000 combined single limit).
electrical.summary: The South Dakota Electrical Commission licenses apprentice electricians, journeymen and electrical contractors. Contractors must post an undertaking and carry public liability insurance; no online license search was found, so homeowners may need to contact the Commission to verify a license.

general_contracting.summary: South Dakota does not issue a statewide general or home improvement contractor license. Licensing, where required, is handled by cities and counties, so homeowners should check with their city or county.

hvac.summary: South Dakota does not issue a statewide HVAC/mechanical contractor license. Licensing, where required, is handled by cities and counties, so homeowners should check with their city or county.

legal.agency: South Dakota Supreme Court / State Bar of South Dakota
legal.summary: To practice law in South Dakota, an attorney must be licensed by the South Dakota Supreme Court and be an active member in good standing of the State Bar of South Dakota.

plumbing.agency: South Dakota Plumbing Commission (Department of Labor and Regulation)
plumbing.summary: The South Dakota Plumbing Commission licenses plumbers, plumbing contractors, and related installers such as sewer and water installers. Licenses expire each December 31, and the Commission publishes lists of current licensees rather than a searchable database.

roofing.summary: South Dakota does not issue a statewide roofing contractor license. Licensing, where required, is handled by cities and counties, so homeowners should check with their city or county.

electrical.agency: Tennessee Board for Licensing Contractors (Department of Commerce & Insurance)
electrical.summary: Tennessee requires a contractor's license from the Board for Licensing Contractors for electrical work of $25,000 or more. The board also issues a Limited Licensed Electrician (LLE) license for smaller electrical jobs.
electrical.threshold: projects of $25,000 or more (including materials, equipment, and labor)

general_contracting.agency: Tennessee Board for Licensing Contractors (Department of Commerce & Insurance)
general_contracting.insurance_bond: Home improvement licensees must provide a $10,000 surety bond (or other approved financial responsibility such as a cash or property bond or irrevocable letter of credit).
general_contracting.summary: Tennessee requires a contractor's license before bidding or contracting on projects of $25,000 or more. Residential remodeling projects from $3,000 to $24,999 require a home improvement license only in counties that have adopted the law: Bradley, Davidson, Hamilton, Haywood, Knox, Marion, Robertson, Rutherford, and Shelby.
general_contracting.threshold: contractor's license for projects of $25,000 or more; home improvement license for residential remodeling of $3,000 to $24,999 in adopting counties

hvac.agency: Tennessee Board for Licensing Contractors (Department of Commerce & Insurance)
hvac.summary: Tennessee requires a contractor's license from the Board for Licensing Contractors for HVAC/mechanical work of $25,000 or more, whether the contractor works directly for the owner or as a subcontractor. For smaller jobs, homeowners should check their city or county's requirements.
hvac.threshold: projects of $25,000 or more (including materials, equipment, and labor)

legal.agency: Board of Professional Responsibility of the Supreme Court of Tennessee
legal.summary: The Board of Professional Responsibility of the Supreme Court of Tennessee runs the online attorney directory for lawyers licensed in Tennessee. Listings show license status (such as active, inactive, or suspended) and any public discipline.

plumbing.agency: Tennessee Board for Licensing Contractors (Department of Commerce & Insurance)
plumbing.summary: Tennessee requires a contractor's license from the Board for Licensing Contractors for plumbing work of $25,000 or more. The board also issues a Limited Licensed Plumber (LLP) license for smaller jobs, which is accepted only in some cities and counties, so homeowners should check local rules.
plumbing.threshold: projects of $25,000 or more (including materials, equipment, and labor)

roofing.agency: Tennessee Board for Licensing Contractors (Department of Commerce & Insurance)
roofing.summary: Tennessee has no separate roofing board; roofing contractors need a contractor's license from the Board for Licensing Contractors when the roofing work is $25,000 or more. In some counties, residential remodeling jobs from $3,000 to $24,999 require a home improvement license.
roofing.threshold: projects of $25,000 or more (including materials, equipment, and labor)

electrical.agency: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation (TDLR)
electrical.summary: Texas requires anyone performing non-exempt electrical work to be licensed by TDLR and to work through a licensed electrical contractor.

general_contracting.summary: Texas has no statewide licensing requirement for general contractors, though some trades (such as electrical, air conditioning, and plumbing) need state licenses. Homeowners should check with their city or county for local registration and permit rules.

hvac.agency: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation (TDLR)
hvac.insurance_bond: Commercial general liability insurance: Class A $300,000 per occurrence / $600,000 aggregate / $300,000 products-completed operations; Class B $100,000 / $200,000 / $100,000
hvac.summary: Texas requires anyone who installs, repairs, or maintains air conditioning, refrigeration, or heating systems to hold a TDLR license. Class A covers any size unit; Class B covers cooling systems of 25 tons and under and heating systems of 1.5 million BTU per hour and under.

legal.summary: Attorneys practicing in Texas are members of the State Bar of Texas. Its Find a Lawyer directory lets the public look up attorneys.

plumbing.agency: Texas State Board of Plumbing Examiners (TSBPE)
plumbing.summary: The Texas State Board of Plumbing Examiners licenses and regulates the plumbing trade in Texas. Its public license search lets homeowners look up a plumber's license.

roofing.summary: Texas has no statewide license requirement for roofing contractors. Homeowners should check with their city or county for any local registration or permit rules.

electrical.agency: Utah Division of Professional Licensing (DOPL), Department of Commerce
electrical.insurance_bond: General liability insurance of at least $1,000,000 per occurrence and $2,000,000 aggregate.
electrical.summary: Utah licenses electrical contractors through DOPL (E200 General Electrical and E201 Residential Electrical classifications), and the qualifier must hold an active Utah master or residential master electrician license. Individual electricians are also licensed by DOPL.

general_contracting.agency: Utah Division of Professional Licensing (DOPL), Department of Commerce
general_contracting.insurance_bond: General liability insurance of at least $1,000,000 per occurrence and $2,000,000 aggregate.
general_contracting.summary: Utah licenses contractors at the state level through DOPL, including B100 General Building and R100 Residential & Small Commercial classifications. Licenses are issued to business entities, which must carry general liability insurance.

hvac.agency: Utah Division of Professional Licensing (DOPL), Department of Commerce
hvac.insurance_bond: General liability insurance of at least $1,000,000 per occurrence and $2,000,000 aggregate.
hvac.summary: Utah licenses HVAC contractors through DOPL under the H100 HVAC contractor classification, which requires the qualifier to pass the H100 trade exam. All licensed contractors must carry general liability insurance.

legal.summary: Lawyers practicing in Utah must be licensed members of the Utah State Bar. The Bar's licensee directory can be used to check whether someone is a licensed Utah attorney.

plumbing.agency: Utah Division of Professional Licensing (DOPL), Department of Commerce
plumbing.insurance_bond: General liability insurance of at least $1,000,000 per occurrence and $2,000,000 aggregate.
plumbing.summary: Utah licenses plumbing contractors through DOPL (P200 General Plumbing and P201 Residential Plumbing classifications), and the qualifier must hold an active Utah master or residential master plumber license. Individual plumbers are also licensed by DOPL.

roofing.agency: Utah Division of Professional Licensing (DOPL), Department of Commerce
roofing.insurance_bond: General liability insurance of at least $1,000,000 per occurrence and $2,000,000 aggregate.
roofing.summary: Utah licenses roofing contractors through DOPL under the S280 Roofing Contractor specialty classification. All licensed contractors must carry general liability insurance.

electrical.agency: Virginia Department of Professional and Occupational Regulation (DPOR), Board for Contractors
electrical.summary: Virginia's Board for Contractors licenses individual electricians at journeyman and master levels. Firms doing electrical work over $1,000 also need a Class A, B, or C contractor license.
electrical.threshold: Class C contractor license required for a single contract or project over $1,000 but less than $30,000 (and less than $250,000 within any 12-month period); Class B and Class A apply to larger amounts.

general_contracting.agency: Virginia Department of Professional and Occupational Regulation (DPOR), Board for Contractors
general_contracting.summary: Virginia requires contractors to hold a Class A, B, or C license from the Board for Contractors; the class sets how large a job they may take on. Home repair and improvement work falls under the Home Improvement Contracting (HIC) classification, among others.
general_contracting.threshold: Class C: single contract or project over $1,000 but less than $30,000, and less than $250,000 within any 12-month period. Class B: $30,000 or more but less than $150,000 per project, or $250,000 or more but less than $1 million in 12 months. Class A: $150,000 or more per project, or $1 million or more in 12 months.

hvac.agency: Virginia Department of Professional and Occupational Regulation (DPOR), Board for Contractors
hvac.summary: Virginia's Board for Contractors licenses individual HVAC tradesmen at journeyman and master levels, with a separate residential HVAC mechanic license. Firms doing HVAC work over $1,000 also need a Class A, B, or C contractor license.
hvac.threshold: Class C contractor license required for a single contract or project over $1,000 but less than $30,000 (and less than $250,000 within any 12-month period); Class B and Class A apply to larger amounts.

legal.summary: Lawyers practicing in Virginia must be members of the Virginia State Bar; active (plenary) members in good standing may practice law. The Bar's lawyer directory shows each attorney's membership status.

plumbing.agency: Virginia Department of Professional and Occupational Regulation (DPOR), Board for Contractors
plumbing.summary: Virginia's Board for Contractors licenses individual plumbers at journeyman and master levels, with a separate residential plumbing license. Firms doing plumbing work over $1,000 also need a Class A, B, or C contractor license.
plumbing.threshold: Class C contractor license required for a single contract or project over $1,000 but less than $30,000 (and less than $250,000 within any 12-month period); Class B and Class A apply to larger amounts.

roofing.agency: Virginia Department of Professional and Occupational Regulation (DPOR), Board for Contractors
roofing.summary: Virginia licenses roofers as contractors under the Board for Contractors, using the Roofing Contracting (ROC) specialty on a Class A, B, or C contractor license.
roofing.threshold: A contractor license is required for a single contract or project over $1,000; Class C covers over $1,000 but less than $30,000 per project (and less than $250,000 within any 12-month period).

electrical.agency: Washington State Department of Labor & Industries (L&I)
electrical.insurance_bond: $4,000 electrical/telecommunication contractor's surety bond, or assignment of savings account.
electrical.summary: Electrical contractors in Washington must hold an L&I electrical contractor license with an assigned certified electrical administrator or master electrician, and electricians must hold an L&I electrician certificate. L&I encourages but does not require liability insurance for electrical contractors.

general_contracting.agency: Washington State Department of Labor & Industries (L&I)
general_contracting.insurance_bond: $30,000 surety bond for general contractors ($15,000 for specialty contractors). General liability insurance of $200,000 public liability and $50,000 property damage, or $250,000 combined single limit.
general_contracting.summary: Washington requires all construction contractors to register with L&I as either general contractors, who can perform most types of construction work and hire subcontractors, or specialty contractors. Registration requires a surety bond and general liability insurance.

hvac.agency: Washington State Department of Labor & Industries (L&I)
hvac.summary: Washington requires all construction contractors, including HVAC contractors, to register with L&I. Electrical work on HVAC and refrigeration equipment requires an L&I electrician certificate, such as the HVAC/refrigeration system (06A) specialty.

legal.summary: Lawyers in Washington are licensed through the Washington State Bar Association. Its Legal Directory shows contact information, license status and public discipline for licensed legal professionals.

plumbing.agency: Washington State Department of Labor & Industries (L&I)
plumbing.summary: L&I certifies plumbers after they complete required on-the-job training hours and pass an exam. Only L&I-certified plumbers can legally do plumbing work on someone else's property; owners may do their own plumbing on property they own.

roofing.agency: Washington State Department of Labor & Industries (L&I)
roofing.insurance_bond: Specialty contractors: $15,000 surety bond; general contractors: $30,000 surety bond. General liability insurance of $200,000 public liability and $50,000 property damage, or $250,000 combined single limit.
roofing.summary: Washington requires all construction contractors to register with L&I; a roofer can register as a specialty contractor, which may only do work in its registered specialty, or as a general contractor.

electrical.agency: Wisconsin Department of Safety and Professional Services (DSPS)
electrical.summary: Wisconsin's DSPS issues Electrical Contractor credentials to businesses and licenses individual electricians (such as master and journeyman electricians). Homeowners can check a credential in DSPS's LicensE license lookup.

general_contracting.agency: Wisconsin Department of Safety and Professional Services (DSPS)
general_contracting.insurance_bond: A bond of at least $25,000 endorsed by a surety authorized in Wisconsin, or a general liability insurance policy of at least $250,000 per occurrence.
general_contracting.summary: Wisconsin requires contractors who obtain building permits for one- and two-family dwelling work to hold a Dwelling Contractor certification from DSPS (homeowners working on their own residence are exempt). The certification requires proof of financial responsibility.

hvac.agency: Wisconsin Department of Safety and Professional Services (DSPS)
hvac.summary: Wisconsin's DSPS issues an HVAC Contractor credential to businesses and an HVAC Qualifier credential to individuals. Homeowners can check a credential in DSPS's LicensE license lookup.

legal.agency: Supreme Court of Wisconsin / State Bar of Wisconsin
legal.summary: The Wisconsin court system directs the public to the State Bar of Wisconsin's Lawyer Search to check whether a lawyer is in good standing. The court's Office of Lawyer Regulation can say whether public discipline has been imposed.

plumbing.agency: Wisconsin Department of Safety and Professional Services (DSPS)
plumbing.summary: Wisconsin licenses plumbers at the state level through DSPS, including master plumber and journeyman plumber credentials. Homeowners can check a credential in DSPS's LicensE license lookup.

roofing.agency: Wisconsin Department of Safety and Professional Services (DSPS)
roofing.summary: Wisconsin has no separate roofing license. Contractors who obtain a building permit for one- and two-family dwelling work must hold the state Dwelling Contractor certification from DSPS (owner-occupants working on their own home are exempt).
